item.title: Airtel’s SmartCash hits 3 million users in Nigeria’s mobile money push
item.description: SmartCash Payment Service Banks (PSB), Airtel Nigeria’s financial services arm, has crossed nearly three million active users as it doubles down on a zero-fee banking model and a market-leading 15% annual interest rate

item.title: Kenyan workers training Meta’s AI glasses say they see users’ most intimate moments
item.description: The report, published on February 27, shines a light on the hidden human labour behind Meta's push into wearable artificial intelligence, and raises fresh questions about data protection, cross-border data transfers, and the psychological toll on content moderators working for Sama in Nairobi.

item.title: Nedbank’s NCBA deal could push some Kenyan institutional investors into cash exit
item.description: Some NCBA shareholders could exit the lender entirely after the transaction is completed, even if other investors become Nedbank shareholders through the stock component of the offer.

item.title: Nomba wants Nigerian merchants to collect pounds directly from UK banks
item.description: The integration with Volume enables merchants to receive bank-to-bank payments from customers that use any of the UK’s major banks, reducing the reliance on international card processors that have dominated cross-border payments. Instead of using card details, customers authorise payments directly from their banking apps.

item.title: Absa Kenya raises government securities holdings 19% as loan demand weakens
item.description: Absa Bank Kenya increased its holdings of government securities by 19% in 2025 as weak loan demand pushed banks to channel more funds into state debt while digital income supported earnings.

item.title: Africa’s crypto is complex. Josephine Inika has made a career simplifying it.
item.description: Inika did not arrive at crypto marketing by design; she arrived by experiment.

item.title: This startup wants to bring Bitcoin to Africans who can’t afford the Internet
item.description: Machankura allows people to send and receive Bitcoin using USSD technology, the same system Africans use to check airtime, transfer mobile money, or query their account balance in traditional banking.
